changes: p1: removed role 'king'. In ŚS 1659 (1737 CE) Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa was only crown prince (yuvarāja, mahārājādhirājakumāra). The reigning king of Gorkha was his father, Narabhūpāla Śāha, who is not named in the colophon. Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa keeps the role 'commissioner' because the copy was made by his order (ājñayā likhitam).

purpose: copied by order (ājñayā) of crown prince Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa Śāha
notes: The colophon writes 'pṛṭhvī' with a retroflex ṭh, a scribal or typing slip for 'pṛthvī'. The text calls Pṛthvīnārāyaṇa yuvarāja / mahārājādhirājakumāra, so in ŚS 1659 (= VS 1794 = 1737 CE) he was crown prince, not king. He took the Gorkha throne in 1743. His father, Narabhūpāla Śāha, was reigning but is not named. 'Dharmādhikaraṇa' (literally 'court of justice') here describes the scribe, so it probably means he held the office of judge (dharmādhikārin) at the Gorkha court. The catalogue's VS 1794 matches ŚS 1659. The weekday has not been checked. No place of copying is stated, although Gorkha is likely.
